title: Tooling: audit unchecked selected dependency heads and add an opt-in consistency guard
body:
## Change and scope

At base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`, the fast selected-record checker accepts four metadata-only mutants: false reviewed heads, false previous kappa, false source PRs, and false publication text. Certificate, source-inventory, and proof-supplement checks remain intact; a corrupted certificate digest is still rejected.

This adds `research/selected-dependency-heads-audit/` with reproducible mutation evidence and an opt-in `guard.py`. The guard rejects the three head/previous-kappa/source-PR mutants and accepts the published record. Publication prose is documented as unchecked; the guard does not establish its correctness.

**Low-severity provenance-metadata audit; no new kappa.** The production checker and selected frontier are unchanged. The guard checks local consistency, not GitHub authenticity or mathematical validity. The published record's 48 reviewed heads remain consistent: 35 shared heads agree with the preceding checkpoint, and 13 agree with the batch1099 integration record.

## Validation

The audit and guard themselves run with Python 3.10+. The registered package runner requires **Python 3.12**.

```sh
python3.12 -B research/selected-dependency-heads-audit/verify.py
python3.12 -B research/selected-dependency-heads-audit/guard.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-dependency-heads-audit
```

Expected statuses: `PASS_SELECTED_DEPENDENCY_HEADS_AUDIT`, `PASS_SELECTED_DEPENDENCY_HEADS_GUARD`, and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. The audit reports four metadata mutants accepted by the existing checker and three rejected by the proposed guard. Normal verification compares the committed `EXPECTED.json` without rewriting it.

The full `make frontier1094-verify` replay was not run. No full-suite, Lean, or multiplication-theorem validation is claimed.

## Sources and attribution

Task: `supplier-boundary-audit`, refined to dependency metadata. `SOURCES.json` pins the consumed files at base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`. This concerns different fields from #1735 / discussion #1730's certificate-to-replay binding. Credit remains with the authors of the selected #1094, frontier1042, batch1099 integration, and predecessor audit/binding packages linked in the README.
